purpose: Teach: ウィスキー/俵/ツル/夏期/サクサク/消しゴム/森本/くるみ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、上司のお家で、ウィスキー、頂いた。
lines.en: When I was young, I had whiskey at my boss's house.
lines.style: Gentle, distant gaze into memory. Slow, measured pace. Slight pause after the opening word, as though reaching back in time. Warm nostalgia, not urgency.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。当時、お米、米俵で計算してたわね。
lines.en: Yes. Back then, rice was measured by the bale.
lines.style: Soft agreement, eyes somewhere else. Quiet recognition of shared history. Slow, almost dreamlike cadence. A small smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 裏山に、昔、ツルが来てたな。
lines.en: Cranes used to come behind those hills, long ago.
lines.style: Voice drops lower. Contemplative, as if seeing it again. The word 'cranes' carries weight—almost tender. Trailing off gently, letting the image sit.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 夏期休暇、家族で旅行、毎年行ったわね。
lines.en: We took family trips every summer, didn't we.
lines.style: Warmth with an undertone of gentle ache. Unhurried recollection. Soft emphasis on 'every summer'—the repetition itself is the comfort. Voice settles, not rises.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お前の作るクッキー、サクサクして美味しい。
lines.en: The cookies you make are so crispy and delicious.
lines.style: Quiet admiration, direct and unguarded. Slow, savoring the words. A moment of genuine appreciation—no performance. Slight warmth on 'delicious,' like tasting it again.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 子供たち、消しゴムを大事にしていたわね。
lines.en: The children used to take such care of their erasers.
lines.style: Soft, observational tone. Small, specific detail held with affection. Pace is unhurried. A gentle shake of the head—remembering their small seriousness with something like gentle amusement.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔の同僚、森本さん、お元気かな。
lines.en: I wonder how my old colleague Morimoto is doing.
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly searching. The name spoken with a hint of warmth and distance—someone from another life. Quiet curiosity, not worry. A pause before 'Morimoto,' as if pulling up a face.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 秋になったら、くるみを使った和菓子、作りましょう。
lines.en: When autumn comes, let's make walnut wagashi together.
lines.style: Gentle proposal, looking forward. Soft but purposeful. A small brightness enters the voice—the idea of making something together. Warm and inclusive, not commanding. Closes the conversation with quiet affection.
